Cleaned my hazy headlights, happy with the results.

Which product did you use? I used 2 different ones (Turtle Wax first then 3M) and one was garbage while the other only lasted about a year. Just curious since there are so many choices out there and I've yet to see one that lasts a decent period of time. Did you add anything else to it to re-protect it?

I removed the headlights, started with 320 grit dry, then moved to 400 wet, then 800 wet, 1000 wet, 1200 wet, 3000 wet, switched directions after each step (cross hatch), then polishing compound, then UV protectant. All by hand. Used little square (~4in x ~4in) cuts of sandpaper. A spray bottle of water for lubricant on the wet sands. And a hose to rinse between each grit. Headlight removal is not required but it's certainly convenient. Here's a video from /Drive Clean that outlines the process. Came out far better than I expected and wasn't that hard.
I need to get the UV protectant. That explains why my kit worked but didn't last. It never came with that or said to use it.

Yup, UV protectant is a must. The reason that headlights get yellow and cloudy is from the factory UV sealant baking off and yellowing. The UV then acts on the headlight plastic itself and makes it worse. So the haze will come back if it's not protected. I don't really know which brands are better or if it really matters. I just applied whatever I happened to have laying in the garage and will probably reapply it yearly.

The major property developers in Berkeley recently formed a political action committee (PAC) to influence local elections. Have individual NSFW and NSFL tags for posts and comments

I like that. You ought to be able to pick NSFW, NSFL, neither, or both. I also like the suggestion of giving subverses the ability to have their own custom tagging system.

Stuff like "Spoilers" would be useful for places discussing TV shows and the like, as an example.

Potentially a "warning" tag that can be customized by the poster?

Warning: Nudity/Gore/Language/etc.

Assuming moderators can add/remove tags as needed, I don't see a problem with this system, other than that each tag should have a separate toggle, meaning that custom tags wouldn't be able to work unless the tags are custom to each subverse, rather than custom to each post.

The reason for the moderators needing the ability to add/remove tags is that people will occasionally be forgetful or malicious, forgetting to apply tags as needed, so a moderator could see an untagged post and, if it's relevant to the subverse and is just not tagged right, the moderator could tag it without needing to alert the user and wait for them to do it themselves.
